questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how the types in this code expose their data to callers? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.

SearchRequest's compact constructor strips and lowercases the text, copies the filters with Set.copyOf and clamps page and pageSize. Besides validation, what does this matter for CachingSearchBackend?
choices: Records cannot be used as cache keys without a compact constructor.
Requests that mean the same thing become equal values, so they share one cache entry.
It lets the cache expire entries by page.

questions.prompt: A new type ExistsFilter is added to the Filter hierarchy (and to the permits clause). What happens to InMemoryBackend.matches, which switches over Filter without a default branch?
choices: It does not compile until a case for ExistsFilter is added.
It compiles and throws MatchException at runtime only for ExistsFilter.
It silently treats ExistsFilter as a TermFilter.
It compiles, and ExistsFilter matches every hit.

questions.prompt: Two identical requests reach CachingSearchBackend at the same moment on a cold cache. How many times is the delegate called?
choices: Twice, because both threads see a miss.
Once per page of the request.
Zero times for the second request, which receives null.
Once: Cache.get(key, loader) computes atomically per key and the second caller waits for the same value.
